## The next session and the reading {#next-session}

::: {.small .nonincremental}
- **The next session** takes up SCORE and its robustness study: the programme that put published claims through all three Rs, the many-analysts study inside it, and what the four case studies of the workshop recorded
- **The reading of this session** is the glossary on the Resources page of the site of your case study, which sets out the four terms of repetition with the place of each in the case study
- The glossary follows the four-page paper by Nosek and colleagues, which is open at the address below [@NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms]

::: notes
That is the vocabulary that the rest of the workshop uses: three kinds of repetition, kept apart, and the practices that make each kind possible for somebody other than the author. Whether published findings hold up when somebody does check them has now been measured on a large scale, and that is the next session. SCORE put hundreds of published findings through all three kinds of repetition, and its robustness study, the many-analysts study inside it, is where the four case studies of this workshop come from. The reading for this session is short: the glossary on the Resources page of the site of your case study, which follows a four-page paper by Nosek and colleagues and says where each term turns up in your case study.
:::
